# Gospel of Judas — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Tchacos, pp. 33-58 | Coptic

---

## The Hidden Gospel: What Jesus Told Only Judas

---

**1** This is the secret teaching — the hidden revelation — that Jesus shared with Judas Iscariot over eight days, in the final three days before Passover.

**2** Jesus had walked among humanity, performing signs and extraordinary wonders to bring salvation to the human race. Some people responded by walking in righteousness; others persisted in transgression. He called twelve disciples to follow him.

**3** He began revealing to them the mysteries hidden beyond this world — what lies at the end of all things. But often he kept himself hidden from them, appearing in their midst only as a child.

**4** One day he came to Judaea and found his disciples gathered together, sitting in solemn religious observance. As he approached them, he saw them assembled around a table, offering prayers of thanksgiving over bread. He laughed.

**5** His disciples said to him: "Teacher, why are you laughing at our prayer? We have done the right thing."

**6** He answered them: "I am not laughing at you. What you are doing — you're not doing it because you chose to. This is what your god demands, and he receives praise through it."

**7** They said: "Master, you are [...] the Son of our God."

**8** Jesus said to them: "How is it that you think you know who I am? I tell you the truth: not one person of your generation will ever truly know me."

**9** When the disciples heard this, anger and distress swept over them, and they began to curse him silently, in their hearts.

**10** Seeing their confusion, Jesus said to them: "Why are you letting this agitation push you into anger? The god you worship — the one living inside you, together with his angels — has stirred up your spirits against me."

**11** "Is there anyone among you strong enough to step forward? Bring out the true, complete human being and stand before me."

**12** They all said: "We can do it!" But not one of them had the courage to stand before him — except Judas Iscariot. He stepped forward, though he could not meet Jesus's eyes; he looked away, turning his face aside.

**13** Judas said: "I know who you are and where you come from. You came from the immortal realm of Barbelo, and the one who sent you — I am not even worthy to speak his name."

**14** Jesus saw that Judas was reaching toward something far beyond the others. He said to him: "Step away from the rest of them. I'm going to tell you the secrets of the Kingdom — not because you will enter it, but because what lies ahead will cost you deeply."

**15** At those words, Judas separated himself from the others, and Jesus took him away privately.

**16** Jesus said to him: "Look up. Gaze at that cloud and the light blazing inside it, and all the stars circling around it. You see that one star leading the procession? That star belongs to you."

**17** Judas looked up and saw the brilliant cloud, and he passed into it. Those left standing below heard a voice ringing out from the cloud, saying: [...]

**18** Jesus returned. He found his disciples gathered together again, sitting in their pious worship.

**19** The disciples said to him: "Teacher, we saw you in a dream last night. We saw a great house with a great altar inside. Twelve men were standing there — priests, we thought. A name was there. And a huge crowd was waiting around that altar."

**20** "We said, 'Teacher, let our priests make their offerings.' And then Jesus said: 'What are you [...] doing?'"

**21** The disciples continued: "Some of those priests fast for two weeks at a time; others sacrifice their own children; others their wives, all in praise and humility among themselves; some sleep with other men; some carry out killings; some commit every kind of sin and lawlessness imaginable. And these are the men who stand before the altar calling out your name."

**22** "And in the midst of all their shortcomings and failures, they still present their sacrifices."

**23** When Jesus heard this he laughed again. He said: "Why are you so troubled? I'm telling you plainly: every single one of those priests who stand before that altar — they invoke my name. And I tell you again: my name has been inscribed upon [...] through the generations of the stars and the human generations. They have planted fruitless trees in my name, in utter disgrace."

**24** Jesus said to them: "You realize what you've just told me, don't you? Those figures you saw standing at the altar receiving the offerings — that is you. That is the god you serve. And those twelve men you saw? That is you. The animals led to sacrifice are all the people you mislead in my name."

**25** "The one who will stand at that altar [...] will use my name this way, and the generations of the devoted will stay loyal to him. After him will come one from the fornicators, and after him one who slays children, another who sleeps with men, those who practice abstinence, and all the rest — people mired in pollution, lawlessness, and delusion, who say, 'We are equals with the angels.' These are the stars rushing everything toward its end. Humanity has been told, 'See — God himself has received your sacrifice through the hands of a priest.' But that priest is a servant of error."

**26** "And yet the Lord — the Lord over all — decrees it: on the last day, they will all face their shame."

**27** Jesus said: "Stop your sacrificing [...] which you have [...] over the altar, since it is all over your stars and your angels, and it has already run its course there. So let them go [...] before you, and let them pass away [...] through the generations. No baker can feed the whole of creation beneath the heavens."

**28** "And [...] to them [...] along with the fountain of wisdom [...] a generation [...] light. In imperishability [...] since [...] came [...]."

**29** The disciples said: "Teacher, you've heard all of this [...] So what advantage have we actually gained? What did our ancestors gain — since they left this life having never laid eyes on the aeons?"

**30** Jesus laughed and said: "What is going on inside you? Why does something [...] grieve within you? Your god who lives inside you [...] with your [...] soul. [...] If there is anyone strong enough here, let that person bring out the perfect human and stand before me."

**31** They all said: "We can do it!" And still not one of them could stand before him — except Judas Iscariot. He stood before Jesus, but he turned his face away.

**32** Judas said: "I know who you are and where you come from. You have come from the immortal realm of Barbelo, and I am not worthy to pronounce the name of the one who sent you."

**33** Seeing that Judas was stretching toward something high and separate, Jesus said to him: "Come away from the others. I will share with you the secrets of the Kingdom. You can reach it — but it will bring you tremendous grief."

**34** "Because someone else will take your place in order to make the twelve complete before their god."

**35** Judas said to him: "When will you tell me these things? When will the great day of light break open for the generation [...]?"

**36** But when he had spoken, Jesus left him. The following morning, Jesus appeared to his disciples again.

**37** They said to him: "Teacher, where did you go? What were you doing while you were away from us?"

**38** Jesus said to them: "I went to be with another generation — a great and holy one."

**39** His disciples said to him: "Lord, who is this great generation, higher than us, holier than us — one that doesn't even exist yet in these realms of the aeons?"

**40** When Jesus heard this, he laughed and said to them: "Why are you puzzling in your hearts over the strong and holy generation?"

**41** "I tell you truly: no one born into this age will ever see that generation. No angelic army of the stars has any power over it. No one of mortal birth can be part of it — because that generation doesn't come from [...] which has become [...] the human generation among [...] power [...] other powers [...] by which you exercise authority."

**42** Each of the disciples was shaken to the core when they heard this. No one could say a word.

**43** On another day, Jesus came to them again. They said to him: "Teacher, we have seen you — in a vision, in great dreams last night."

**44** He said: "Why have you [...] Why have you been hiding?"

**45** They said: "We saw a great house, and inside it a great altar, and twelve men — the ones we call the priests. And a name and a huge crowd of people gathered around the altar."

**46** Jesus said: "I tell you the truth: that crowd pressing around the altar and invoking that name — that is your priesthood. [...] He will stand at the altar and use my name this way, and those who are devoted will stay loyal to him generation after generation."

**47** "After him will come a man from among the fornicators, then one who slays children, then one who sleeps with men, those who practice abstinence, and all the rest — people of corruption, lawlessness, and delusion who say: 'We are equal to the angels.' These are the very stars driving everything to its final end. For humanity has been told: 'Look — God received your sacrifice through the hands of a priest.' That priest is nothing but a servant of error."

**48** "But the Lord — the Lord over all — he himself will be put to shame on the final day."

**49** Jesus said to them: "Stop [...]. [...] Your god will not be saved [...] generations will [...] the rulers [...] But I tell you, [...] the angel who [...] the holy ones and the generation [...] the light."

**50** Jesus said all of these things. Then he took Judas aside privately and said to him:

**51** "Come with me. I am going to show you things that no human being has ever seen. There is a great and infinite aeon — no generation of angels has ever measured its extent. Inside it dwells the great invisible Spirit. No angel's eye has seen it. No thought has ever reached it. It has never been called by any name."

**52** "And then a brilliant cloud appeared there. Out of that cloud came a voice: 'Let an angel come into being — one who will serve me.' And out of the cloud emerged a great angel, the divine Light itself — the Self-Generated One. Because of him, four more angels came out of another cloud, and these became servants of the angelic Self-Generated One."

**53** "And the Self-Generated One declared, 'Let [...] come into being [...],' and it came to be. And he created the first luminary to reign. He commanded, 'Let angels come into being and serve him,' and countless myriads came to be. He proclaimed, 'Let a luminous aeon come into being,' and it was so."

**54** "He created a second great luminary to reign, along with countless myriads of angels to serve. This is how he brought the rest of the aeons of light into being — establishing them as sovereigns, surrounding each with untold myriads of angels."

**55** "Adamas dwelt in the first luminous cloud — a cloud that no angel among those called 'God' had ever seen. He [...] the image [...] and fashioned after the likeness of that angel. And he brought into being the incorruptible generation of Seth — twelve aeons for twelve luminaries. And twenty-four luminaries in their generation — that is, seventy-two luminaries within each aeon — and their power [...]."

**56** "Then Saklas said to his angels: 'Let us make a human being in our likeness, in our image.' And they fashioned Adam, and they fashioned his wife Eve — in the cloud she is called Zoe, which means Life. All the generations have come looking for him by this name, and each calls her by her own names. Now Saklas did not [...] give the command except to [...] the generations [...] And the ruler said to Adam: 'You shall live long, together with your children.'"

**57** Judas said to Jesus: "But [how] long will humanity actually live?"

**58** Jesus said: "Why are you so surprised? The lifespan of Adam and his whole line — the entire number fixed as the limit under the reign of Saklas — all of it was set from the beginning. After that time runs out, that generation will be raised up, and your star will lead the way. Think carefully about what you are about to do. I tell you the truth: your final days [...] weep [...] the archon will be destroyed [...] and then the image of the great generation of Adam will be lifted high — for before heaven, before earth, before the angels even existed, that generation was already alive in the eternal realms. Now you know everything. Lift your eyes — look at that cloud, look at the light blazing within it, look at all the stars circling around it. The star leading the procession — that one is yours." Judas lifted his eyes and saw the luminous cloud, and he stepped into it. Those who remained on the ground heard a voice ringing out from the cloud, saying: [...] great generation [...] image [...] And Judas could no longer see Jesus. At once, a commotion broke out among the Jews. [...] Their high priest and the others said: "He has gone into the guest room to pray." Some scribes had been watching, waiting to seize him during the prayer — they feared the crowd, because everyone considered Jesus a prophet. They went to Judas. "What are you doing here? Aren't you a disciple of Jesus?" He told them what they wanted to hear. And Judas took the money and handed Jesus over to them.

---

*Source: Codex Tchacos, pp. 33–58. Coptic. Published 2006 by National Geographic Society; Kasser, Meyer, Wurst, eds. Damaged text indicated by [...]. This text presents Judas's betrayal as a divinely commissioned act of liberation — freeing the divine spark from its material prison — in direct contrast to the canonical gospel tradition.*
